originShared.text: None of these states is one of CSLB's reciprocal-agreement states (Arizona, Louisiana, Mississippi, Nevada, North Carolina) or on CSLB's Reciprocal Classifications List, so no reciprocity trade-exam waiver applies. California's other exam waiver (Business and Professions Code §7065.1) applies only to qualifiers of licenses issued by CSLB itself, not to out-of-state licenses. File CSLB's Application for Original Contractor License (form 13A-1) with the $450 non-refundable application fee, documenting at least four years of journey-level (or higher) C-36 experience within the last 10 years on CSLB's Certification of Work Experience form. Experience from your state can count, but must be documented on CSLB's own form. CSLB's NASCLA exam waiver does not help: it is restricted to the B-General Building classification and does not cover C-36.
Once the application is posted, pass the C-36 trade exam and the California Law and Business exam; exam fees are paid directly to the testing vendor and are not published in the application.
